meta.name: MoorAI Threat Rule-Base
meta.description: AI-security threat matrix for office workers, translated to English. Each threat is a detection rule: example = trigger context, response = intervention. riskScore = severity x likelihood.

schema.atlas: string | string[] — every MITRE ATLAS (v2026.09) technique the rule genuinely implements. A technique is credited only when the rule describes a distinct implemented mechanism that addresses that technique definition; never for a restatement, superset, subset, or downstream consequence of an id already credited on the same rule. Read it through data/atlas.js atlasIds() — never `t.atlas === id` and never a bare interpolation.
schema.atlasPartial: optional { techniqueId: limit } — a credit that is bounded. The technique is implemented, but only over part of what its ATLAS definition covers, and the short limit phrase is the one the public comparison page prints. Every key must also appear in `atlas`.
schema.owaspAgentic: string[] — every OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026) risk, ASI01–ASI10, the rule's own mechanism addresses. Always an array; [] is a reviewed "no credit". Ids and titles: data/owasp-frameworks.js.
schema.owaspAgenticPartial: optional { ASIxx: limit } — a bounded credit, as atlasPartial: the risk is addressed only over part of what the OWASP entry covers. Every key must also appear in owaspAgentic.
schema.owaspMcp: string[] — every OWASP MCP Top 10 (2025, beta) risk, MCP01–MCP10, the rule's own mechanism addresses. Always an array; [] is a reviewed "no credit". Ids and titles: data/owasp-frameworks.js.
schema.owaspMcpPartial: optional { MCPxx: limit } — a bounded credit, as atlasPartial. Every key must also appear in owaspMcp.
schema.attack: { id, coverage, reason }[] — every MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise v20 technique the threat genuinely corresponds to. coverage: full (a shipped mechanism addresses the technique as an AI agent MoorAI watches performs it), partial (part of it; reason states the bound) or none (the technique corresponds, but MoorAI ships no runtime mechanism for it). Coverage is a mechanism claim, not a detection rate. Always an array; [] is a reviewed "no technique corresponds". Ids come from data/attack-v20-techniques.json; read the tag through data/attack.js. Optional on a partial credit: bound "design" with a one-line boundReason when the forms it does not catch are indistinguishable from an agent's legitimate work or outside anything an agent-side hook, proxy or gateway observes; bound "gap", or no field, when MoorAI has not built the detection. Read it through data/attack.js attackBound().
schema.attackNote: string, present only when `attack` is [] — one line on why no ATT&CK v20 technique corresponds to the threat.
schema.cwe: { id, title }[] — every MITRE CWE (4.20) weakness the threat exploits. id is the integer CWE number; title is MITRE's exact entry name, from data/cwe-capec.js CWE_TITLES. A weakness is credited only when it is the one the threat exploits, never one the threat's outcome would introduce (insecure generated code contains CWE-89; it does not exploit it) and never a superset or consequence of an id already credited. Base or Variant entries are preferred; no category, view, deprecated entry, or entry MITRE marks DISCOURAGED for mapping (CWE-1426). Always an array; [] is a reviewed "no honest mapping".
schema.cweNote: string, present only when `cwe` is [] — one line on why no CWE weakness is credited (a person's own sharing or reliance on an answer is not a software weakness).
schema.capec: { id, title }[] — every MITRE CAPEC (3.9) attack pattern the threat is. id is the integer CAPEC number; title is the canonical name, from data/cwe-capec.js CAPEC_TITLES. Credited only when the pattern describes the threat itself, not the condition it uses or what follows it; a Meta pattern only where no Standard or Detailed pattern fits. Always an array; [] is a reviewed "no honest mapping".
schema.capecNote: string, present only when `capec` is [] — one line on why no CAPEC attack pattern is credited (no adversary acts, or CAPEC has no pattern for it, as for prompt injection).
